title: Register the coordination command kind so typed envelopes cross MCP
description:
Objective: make the daemon's coordination surface reachable by an authenticated MCP command, so typed session and terminal envelopes cross a real boundary instead of existing only inside their own directory. GAP C of the Foundation self-host canary (task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a).

MEASURED GAP at HEAD e881141, re-verified independently and unchanged:
- `createCoordinationAdapter` is defined at `apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts:111`, taking `{clock, projectId, store}` and composing `createSessionAuthority` plus `createRecipientRegistry`. Its COMPLETE caller set is `coordination-adapter.test.ts:25,84,90`. Zero production callers.
- The whole directory is unreachable: `grep -rn "coordination/" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src`, filtered to exclude `apps/daemon/src/coordination/` itself and test files, returns ZERO lines. No production daemon module imports anything from it.
- `daemon-command-registry.ts` admits exactly four families — `BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY` (:48), `REVIEW_FAMILY` (:56), `SESSION_FAMILY` (:61, session.open/renew/close, credential lifecycle only), `WORK_FAMILY` (:66) — plus effect.activate and recovery.complete. There is NO coordination or terminal envelope kind, so no MCP client can send or read a typed advisory envelope.
- Note the near-miss that makes this easy to mis-scope: `SESSION_FAMILY` already exists and is about session CREDENTIAL lifecycle. It is not the coordination envelope surface, and extending it instead of adding the coordination kind would leave the gap in place while looking like progress.

Deliverable: a coordination command kind registered in `daemon-command-registry.ts`, backed by `createCoordinationAdapter`, carrying typed addressed envelopes with an authenticated command receipt per state change. Advisory text stays advisory: an envelope's free-form content can never grant command, capability, policy, lease, approval or execution authority, and `advisoryOnly: true` must survive the round trip.

NOT in scope: changing the coordination adapter's internals, the session-authority or recipient-registry semantics, the restart reconciliation wiring (GAP B, its own task), the pinned Claude spawn (GAP A, owned by the ff589 -> 32eddfd3 -> 75ee4a84 -> 6cbff010 chain plus task-d7b352e1), or the canary journey itself.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts, one new coordination command module plus its .js bridge, and their tests. Do NOT edit apps/daemon/src/coordination/** — it is complete and this task is the consumer edge.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "createCoordinationAdapter" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns a PRODUCTION call site in addition to its own definition, and the coordination directory is no longer unreachable: a grep for `coordination/` imports from production daemon modules outside that directory returns at least one line. Both counts were zero before this task.

A registry test sends a typed coordination envelope through the same authenticated command path every other family uses and asserts a real command receipt is produced; the envelope's payload is read back and matches what was sent.

Advisory text carries NO authority: a test sends an envelope whose free-form content names a command kind, a capability, a lease and an approval, and asserts none of them takes effect and that `advisoryOnly: true` survives the round trip unchanged.

Every refusal pins the exact stable code AND the answering layer — unauthenticated sender, revoked or non-live recipient, cross-project recipient, malformed envelope, oversized payload. Where session authority and the coordination layer can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the session layer so the coordination layer is provably the one that answered.

The new kind does not widen an existing family: a test asserts `SESSION_FAMILY` still holds exactly its three credential-lifecycle kinds, so the coordination kind was added rather than smuggled into the session surface.

A mutation removing the registry entry turns a NAMED test red, and a mutation letting advisory text set a real field turns a different NAMED test red — proving both the edge and the advisory-only boundary are load-bearing.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately; the test leg prints a nonzero Test Files/Tests count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta intersected with the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: This is a CONSUMER EDGE task. Do not modify apps/daemon/src/coordination/** — the adapter, session authority and recipient registry are complete and separately tested. If the adapter genuinely cannot be composed as written, report blocked rather than editing it.

Add a COORDINATION kind; do not extend SESSION_FAMILY. That family is session credential lifecycle (open/renew/close) and reusing it would leave the coordination gap in place while appearing to close it.

Free-form text is advisory and can never bypass command authority — no envelope content may grant a command, capability, policy, lease, approval or execution right. Every state change needs its own authenticated command receipt.
Official MCP transports only; no custom dialect. The kind travels the same authenticated command path as every other family.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND TAKE THE TWO DECISIONS THIS PLAN SETTLES. Re-measure at current HEAD first (measured at 0f19e06).
THE GAP IS REAL AND UNCHANGED: `createCoordinationAdapter` (coordination/coordination-adapter.ts:111) has three callers, all in `coordination-adapter.test.ts`; a grep for `coordination/` imports from production daemon modules OUTSIDE that directory returns ZERO. The registry (daemon-command-registry.ts, 320 lines) admits BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY (:48), REVIEW_FAMILY (:56), SESSION_FAMILY (:61), WORK_FAMILY (:66) plus effect.activate and recovery.complete. No coordination kind.
DECISION 1 — WHICH KINDS. `CoordinationAdapter` (:81-91) exposes `send`, `acknowledge`, `read`, `replay`, `authenticate`, `recipients`, `resolveRecipient`, `resolveEffectBinding`, `sessions`. Register EXACTLY the two STATE CHANGES as command kinds: `coordination.send` and `coordination.acknowledge`. `read` and `replay` are reads and must NOT become registry kinds — every registry kind mints a durable command decision, and a read that writes a decision record is a defect, not a feature. If the canary later needs a read path, it goes through the affordance/read surface; say so rather than quietly adding a third kind.
DECISION 2 — WHICH CAPABILITY. `CAPABILITIES` (:43-46) has exactly five: ADMIN `project.admin`, GOAL, PLANNING, REVIEW, WORK. Gate both coordination kinds on `CAPABILITIES.WORK` — coordination traffic runs between coder sessions and wrappers, which is work-adjacent; ADMIN is project/policy/session-LIFECYCLE and gating envelope traffic on it would hand every sender project-admin reach. Do NOT mint a sixth capability: that widens the authority model and is a separate decision. Assert `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` (:120) still lists exactly those five.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained (only the last status survives), never piped into tail (tail's status is reported): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and every failing file as your before-set. Both are expected RED from foreign in-flight slices; repair none of it.

TDD RED, PART 1 — the edge itself. Create the command module's test alongside the not-yet-existing module and let it fail to resolve. Then pin, each refusal asserting the exact stable `COORDINATION_CODES` member AND the answering `COORDINATION_LAYERS` member — both frozen vocabularies already exist at packages/coordination/src/coordination-contracts.ts:28 and :25, so nothing here needs a new code.
Cases: a well-formed `coordination.send` through the SAME authenticated command path every other family uses produces a real command receipt, and the envelope read back matches what was sent; `coordination.acknowledge` likewise; an unauthenticated sender is refused; a revoked or non-live recipient is refused; a cross-project recipient is refused; a malformed envelope is refused; an envelope exceeding `COORDINATION_LIMITS.maxEnvelopeBytes` (65_536) is refused.
WHERE TWO LAYERS CAN ANSWER — session authority and coordination — build the fixture VALID at the session layer so the coordination layer is provably the one that refused. `createCoordinationAdapter` composes `createSessionAuthority` and `createRecipientRegistry` internally, so an unauthenticated fixture will be answered by session authority and would silently stop testing coordination.
Also pin DECISION 1 as a test: assert the registry admits `coordination.send` and `coordination.acknowledge` and does NOT admit a read or replay kind — named explicitly, so a later addition of a read-as-command reddens here rather than quietly minting decision records for reads.

TDD RED, PART 2 — advisory text carries NO authority, which is the epic's own product decision and the reason this surface exists at all. Two production guards already exist and MUST be used rather than reimplemented: `COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` (coordination-contracts.ts:43) lists 19 names — apiKey, argv, authorization, bearer, cmd, command, credential, credentialId, eval, exec, password, privateKey, proof, script, secret, sessionCredential, shell, spawn, token — and `COORDINATION_LIMITS` (:49) bounds advisory bytes, text bytes, data depth, handoff entries, page size, TTL and send attempts.
Write a SWEEP over all 19 forbidden field names, asserting a positive generated-case count so a sweep that silently produces zero passes cannot happen, and asserting each is refused with its exact code and layer. Then the semantic case the field list alone cannot catch: send an envelope whose free-form advisory content NAMES a command kind, a capability, a lease and an approval in ordinary prose, and assert none of them takes effect — no command is admitted, no capability granted, no lease taken, no approval recorded — and that `advisoryOnly: true` survives the round trip unchanged.
Also assert the SERVER-FACT boundary the registry already documents at daemon-command-registry.ts:194-196: project, principal, kind, schema version and decision time are assembled by `requestOf`, never copied from the caller, and "a payload carrying them is refused by the seam's allow-list rather than trusted". Send a payload carrying each of those five and assert the refusal rather than silent overwrite — a silently-ignored spoofed field is indistinguishable from an honoured one at the call site.

IMPLEMENT THE COMMAND MODULE. Create `apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-command.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./coordination-command.ts";`, LF ending — apps/daemon requires a physical bridge per production module and the guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line lands it in `wrongContent`).
It exposes handlers for the two kinds, each taking the assembled server request and delegating to `createCoordinationAdapter(...).send` / `.acknowledge`. Return the adapter's own `CoordinationSendResult` / `CoordinationAckResult` (coordination-contracts.ts:169,172) with code and layer intact — do NOT re-stamp a coordination refusal into a registry-local vocabulary, which would erase which layer answered.
Do NOT modify anything under apps/daemon/src/coordination/ other than adding this module: `coordination-adapter.ts`, `recipient-registry.ts` and `recipient-registry-records.ts` are complete and separately tested. This task is the consumer edge; if the adapter genuinely cannot be composed as written, report blocked rather than editing it.
The adapter takes exactly `{clock, projectId, store}`, and `createDaemonCommandPorts` already has all three in scope — it builds `createSessionAuthority(store, {clock: authorityClock, projectId})` the same way (daemon-command-registry.ts:205-209). Construct the adapter ONCE per port composition, not per command: a per-command adapter would rebuild the session authority and recipient registry on every envelope.
Keep the module under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). Do NOT publish it from apps/daemon/src/index.ts — index-surface.test.ts pins an exact export count and index.ts is not an owned path here.

WIRE THE REGISTRY — four edits, and this is the step that actually closes the gap. In `daemon-command-registry.ts` (320 of a 400 split rail — measure with `grep -c ''` after editing):
(1) Add a `COORDINATION_FAMILY` map alongside the four existing families, mapping `coordination.send` and `coordination.acknowledge` to `CAPABILITIES.WORK`. Add it as its OWN family — do not extend `SESSION_FAMILY`, which is session credential lifecycle (open/renew/close) and would leave this gap in place while appearing to close it.
(2) Add both kinds to the `WiredCommandKind` union (:71-73).
(3) Handle them in `agentCapabilitiesFor` (:75) following the shape the existing single kinds use.
(4) Compose the adapter in `createDaemonCommandPorts` (:196) and route the two kinds to the step-4 handlers through `entryOf`, which already branches per-kind for `EFFECT_ACTIVATE_COMMAND_KIND` and `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_COMMAND_KIND` — mirror that shape rather than inventing a new dispatch path.
The request MUST come from `requestOf`, which assembles commandId, correlationId, decidedAt, expectedVersion, kind, payload, principalId, projectId and schemaVersion as server facts. Do not build a coordination-specific request that copies any of those from the caller.
If the file would cross 400 lines, split the family/handler wiring into a sibling module with its own one-line LF bridge rather than compressing — but check first: four small additions to a 320-line file should land near 350.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove the edge and the advisory boundary are load-bearing. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) Remove the `COORDINATION_FAMILY` entry for `coordination.send` from the registry; a NAMED test must redden — this is the edge itself, so if nothing reddens the registry test never actually exercised the wired path. (2) Make the handler treat one `COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` name as ordinary data; the sweep case for that field must redden on its exact code and layer, proving the sweep reads the production list rather than a copy. (3) Let advisory content set a real field — have the handler copy the advisory's named capability into the granted set; the semantic advisory test must redden, proving the boundary is asserted rather than merely intended. (4) Have the handler copy `principalId` from the caller payload instead of taking `requestOf`'s server fact; the spoofed-server-fact case must redden — and note it must redden on a REFUSAL, not on a silent overwrite, since a silently-ignored spoof is indistinguishable from an honoured one at the call site. (5) Re-stamp one coordination refusal into a registry-local code; a NAMED test must redden on the lost layer.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not on an unrelated compile error. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand — a hand restore goes ambiguous) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit a drill left on disk.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT. Legs, each run separately with its own captured exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` reading the `Test Files`/`Tests` COUNT LINE rather than the exit code (exit 0 with no count line ran nothing). Both stay RED from the foreign slices recorded in step 1. Apply the path-attributed baseline — HEAD failing paths minus merge-base failing paths, intersected with your four owned files, MUST be empty — and quote the remaining foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths.
PROVE THE GAP CLOSED, both greps that returned zero at step 1: `grep -rn "createCoordinationAdapter" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` now returns a production call site beyond its own definition, and a grep for `coordination/` imports from production daemon modules outside that directory now returns at least one line. Quote both.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: (a) is `COORDINATION_FAMILY` its own family, with `SESSION_FAMILY` still holding exactly its three credential-lifecycle kinds? (b) are exactly two kinds registered, with no read or replay kind minting decision records? (c) is `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` still exactly the five existing capabilities — no sixth minted? (d) do coordination refusals carry their own code AND layer, unwrapped? (e) is the adapter constructed ONCE per port composition rather than per command? (f) does the handler use `COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` and `COORDINATION_LIMITS` from the contracts rather than a local copy? (g) are the five server facts taken from `requestOf` and a caller-supplied one REFUSED rather than silently ignored? (h) is apps/daemon/src/coordination/** otherwise unmodified? (i) is every production file under 250 lines, the registry under 400, and the bridge exactly one LF line? (j) does `git status --porcelain` show only the four owned paths with every drill reverted?
Commit by explicit pathspec naming the four files — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`; the index is shared state in this single working directory. Verify with `git show --stat`. In the completion: quote the count lines and both closing greps verbatim, name the test that reddened for each drill, and record that this closes GAP C of canary task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a, which is blocked on it. Keep verification.command under 500 characters.

comments.content:
RE-SCOPE MEASUREMENT, architect-27b64950 at HEAD 381c025. Answer: **option (2)** — no existing surface honestly carries gap C, so it is extra-design for M5.

THE CLOSED UNION, confirmed independently of the worker's report. `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85) is a frozen ~90-member list gating `RuntimeCommandEnvelope.commandKind` (runtime-envelope.ts:25). Read in full, it contains NO coordination or terminal envelope kind; `session.open/renew/close/rotate` are credential lifecycle, and the nearest neighbours (`journal.append`, `step.checkpoint`) are work-progress records, not addressed envelopes. So the worker's finding holds: decode refuses before the registry is read, one seam only, and a registry entry alone is permanently unreachable.

CANDIDATE 1 — chat / message channel layer. DOES NOT EXIST IN moe-next. `grep -rln "chat|message-channel|Channel" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src packages` returns exactly: apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts and packages/coordination/src/index.ts (the unreachable subject itself), plus packages/runner Windows frame/broker/session internals that are process plumbing. There is no chat surface to carry anything. The chat this board runs on belongs to the TRANSITIONAL daemon, which epic rail 2 puts outside moe-next.

CANDIDATE 2 — daemon plugin WS (ws://127.0.0.1:9876/). DOES NOT EXIST IN moe-next, and is forbidden twice over. `grep -rn "9876|WebSocket|websocket"` across apps and packages returns one hit: `apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts:27`, which says "no custom WebSocket, and no alternate lifecycle." The canary's own task rail says "Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect." That port belongs to the transitional daemon.

WHY THAT SETTLES IT. Gap C's requirement (comment-90116e38, third capability) is typed session and terminal communication crossing MCP with a SEPARATE AUTHENTICATED COMMAND RECEIPT per state change. The receipt half is the binding one: the only thing in moe-next that mints an authenticated command receipt is the daemon command registry, and the registry is gated by the closed union. Every alternative carrier either does not exist or cannot produce a receipt. With union expansion ruled out for M5, the capability is out of design for this milestone — not merely unimplemented.

RECOMMENDATION for the human to record:
1. Descope gap C from canary task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a. Its prerequisite list then shrinks by this id, leaving GAP A (task-6cbff010 + task-d7b352e1) and GAP B (task-3e54b466, itself blocked on task-48c0c0db).
2. Archive or park THIS task for a post-M5 epic that owns the `RuntimeCommandKind` expansion and the client regeneration it implies. It is a real capability, just not one M5 can carry.

ONE THING I WILL NOT ASSUME. The canary's DoD 3 names "typed session/terminal communication with exact receipts". Descoping gap C NARROWS that DoD, and narrowing an acceptance DoD is exactly what the Clause-2 rail forbids an architect from doing unilaterally. So this is a recommendation with its evidence, not an action — the human records the descope, or tells me the union expansion is back on the table for M5 and I plan it as a prerequisite instead.

Foreign baseline red (activation-run-commit.test.ts TS2307 x4, untracked peer WIP) is unrelated and unchanged.

comments.content: ARCHIVED by governor-1a5aca5d 12:22Z under the human's standing needed/rescope/delete sweep directive, executing the human's earlier v1-closed ruling to its measured conclusion. The architect's re-scope (comment-123612cc) answered option (2): NO existing surface honestly carries coordination (closed RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS union, decode-refuses-before-registry, design doc silent on coordination — zero occurrences), so this capability is EXTRA-DESIGN for M5. The canary (97554) has been descoped from this prerequisite (its comment-6785a05f records the shrunk list). This task becomes a DESIGN-REVISION MARKER: if a future design revision adds a coordination operation to the command surface, un-archive via set_task_status ARCHIVED→BACKLOG and re-plan against the revised vocabulary — the worker's unreachability proof (compiled probe, TS2322 on both kinds) and the architect's required-edits list (runtime-vocabulary.ts:85 +2 kinds, generated-client regeneration with digest re-pin, mcp/core derived edits) remain valid starting points on this record.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Extend `SESSION_FAMILY` with the coordination kinds. REJECTED and called out in the task rails, because it is the most available wrong answer: SESSION_FAMILY is session CREDENTIAL lifecycle (session.open/renew/close) and reusing it would leave the coordination surface exactly as unreachable while the diff looks like progress. The DoD pins SESSION_FAMILY at exactly three kinds so the substitution reddens.

2) Register all four adapter operations — send, acknowledge, read, replay — as command kinds. REJECTED: every registry kind mints a durable command decision, so registering the reads would write decision records for reads. That is a defect wearing the shape of completeness. Two state changes only, with the reads' absence asserted.

3) Mint a sixth capability, e.g. `coordination.write`. REJECTED for now: it widens the authority model, changes `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES`, and is a decision with blast radius beyond this task. WORK fits the actual traffic (coder sessions and wrappers). If a later task shows WORK is too broad, narrowing it is a contained follow-up; minting it speculatively here is not.

4) Gate on `CAPABILITIES.ADMIN`. REJECTED: ADMIN is project.admin — project/policy/session lifecycle. Gating envelope traffic on it would give every participant able to send a message the same capability that installs policy and activates projects.

5) Re-stamp coordination refusals into a registry-local vocabulary for a uniform command-layer error shape. REJECTED: `COORDINATION_CODES` and `COORDINATION_LAYERS` already exist precisely so a caller can tell WHICH layer refused, and the adapter composes session authority beneath it. Flattening erases the distinction the two vocabularies exist to preserve.

6) Re-implement the forbidden-field and limit checks in the command handler. REJECTED: `COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` (19 names) and `COORDINATION_LIMITS` are production constants; a local copy drifts the day one is added, and the sweep would then be testing the copy. Import them and sweep over the real list.

7) Build the adapter per command for simpler wiring. REJECTED: it rebuilds `createSessionAuthority` and `createRecipientRegistry` on every envelope. Construct once per port composition, where the registry already builds its session authority.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 0f19e06. I filed this task from the canary's GAP C audit; planning it required measuring shapes the audit did not need, and two of those measurements turn into decisions this plan settles.

THE GAP, re-confirmed: `createCoordinationAdapter` (coordination/coordination-adapter.ts:111) has exactly three callers, all in `coordination-adapter.test.ts`. A grep for `coordination/` imports from production daemon modules OUTSIDE that directory returns ZERO lines. The directory is unreachable from production.

THE ADAPTER SURFACE (:81-91): `send`, `acknowledge`, `read`, `replay`, `authenticate`, `recipients`, `resolveRecipient`, `resolveEffectBinding`, `sessions`. It takes exactly `{clock, projectId, store}` (:56) and internally composes `createSessionAuthority` and `createRecipientRegistry` — which is why an unauthenticated fixture is answered by SESSION authority, not coordination, and would silently stop testing the subject.

THE VOCABULARY IS ALREADY COMPLETE in packages/coordination/src/coordination-contracts.ts, so nothing here needs a new code: `COORDINATION_ENVELOPE_VERSION` (:5), `COORDINATION_SCOPE` = "moe:coordination" (:8), `COORDINATION_ENDPOINTS` (:10), `COORDINATION_ENVELOPE_KINDS` (:13), `COORDINATION_ROLES` (:16), `COORDINATION_CONTROL_KINDS` (:21), `COORDINATION_LAYERS` (:25), `COORDINATION_CODES` (:28), `COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` (:43, NINETEEN names), `COORDINATION_LIMITS` (:49, maxEnvelopeBytes 65_536, maxAdvisoryUtf8Bytes 4_096, maxDataDepth 8, maxHandoffEntries 32, maxPageSize 32, maxSendAttempts 8, maxTtlMilliseconds 86_400_000). Result types `CoordinationSendResult` (:169) and `CoordinationAckResult` (:172).

THERE IS NO COORDINATION COMMAND KIND ANYWHERE. `grep COMMAND_KIND` over packages/coordination and apps/daemon/src/coordination returns only `RecipientCommandKind` = REGISTER|REPLACE|REVOKE (recipient-registry-records.ts:29), which is the registry's INTERNAL vocabulary, not an MCP command kind. So the kind must be minted here — that is DECISION 1 and it is genuinely this task's to make.

DECISION 1, taken: register exactly the two STATE CHANGES, `coordination.send` and `coordination.acknowledge`. `read`/`replay` stay out: every registry kind mints a durable command decision, and a read that writes a decision record is a defect. Step 2 pins their ABSENCE so a later read-as-command reddens.

DECISION 2, taken: gate both on `CAPABILITIES.WORK`. The registry has exactly five capabilities (:43-46) — ADMIN `project.admin`, GOAL, PLANNING, REVIEW, WORK. Coordination runs between coder sessions and wrappers, which is work-adjacent; ADMIN covers project/policy/session-LIFECYCLE, so gating envelope traffic on it would hand every sender project-admin reach. Minting a sixth capability widens the authority model and is a separate decision, so `OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES` (:120) must stay exactly five.

REGISTRY SHAPE to mirror, not reinvent: families are `Readonly<Record<Kind, capability>>` (:48, :56, :61, :66); `WiredCommandKind` unions them plus the two singleton kinds (:71-73); `agentCapabilitiesFor` (:75) branches for singletons; `entryOf` inside `createDaemonCommandPorts` (:196) already branches on `kind === EFFECT_ACTIVATE_COMMAND_KIND` and `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_COMMAND_KIND`. `createDaemonCommandPorts` ALREADY has `{clock, projectId, store}` in scope and already builds `createSessionAuthority(store, {clock: authorityClock, projectId})` at :205-209 — so composing the adapter there is cheap and natural, and it must happen ONCE per port composition rather than per command.

THE SERVER-FACT BOUNDARY IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED at :194-196: `requestOf` assembles commandId, correlationId, decidedAt, expectedVersion, kind, payload, principalId, projectId, schemaVersion, and the comment states "a payload carrying them is refused by the seam's allow-list rather than trusted". REFUSED, not overwritten — step 3 pins that distinction because a silently-ignored spoof is indistinguishable from an honoured one at the call site.

LINE BUDGET: daemon-command-registry.ts is 320 of 400. Four small additions should land near 350, but measure.
planningNotes.risks:
1) `SESSION_FAMILY` IS A DECOY and the single most likely way this task ships without closing anything. It exists, it is session-shaped, and extending it compiles. The DoD pins its cardinality at three so the substitution reddens rather than passing review.

2) READS MUST NOT BECOME COMMANDS. Adding `coordination.read` looks like completeness and silently starts minting durable decision records for reads. Step 2 asserts their absence by name.

3) THE UNAUTHENTICATED FIXTURE IS ANSWERED BY THE WRONG LAYER. `createCoordinationAdapter` composes `createSessionAuthority` internally, so a fixture that is invalid at the session layer never reaches coordination and the assertion quietly detaches. Build every coordination-layer fixture VALID at the session layer.

4) A SPOOFED SERVER FACT MUST BE REFUSED, NOT IGNORED. The registry comment says refused; a handler that silently overwrites principalId or projectId looks identical at the call site to one that honoured them. Drill 4 requires the red to land on a refusal.

5) THE FORBIDDEN-FIELD SWEEP CAN GO VACUOUS. Nineteen names; assert a positive generated-case count and import the production list, or the sweep tests a stale copy — or nothing at all.
